svg.data-steps: ["Unit 1, weeks 1 to 5. By the end of it you can trace the founding story back to the sources it actually descends from, and say what the surviving record cannot show.","Unit 2, weeks 6 to 10. By the end of it you can explain how the profession won legal and institutional standing without the scientific question ever being settled.","Unit 3, weeks 11 to 15. By the end of it you can sort a modern claim into the right evidence band and say what a consent conversation has to name.","All three together. Each unit assumes the one before it, and the capstone position paper asks you to argue from the whole record rather than from the part of it you found congenial."]
svg.aria-label: The course runs as three units of five weeks each, origins, legitimacy and evidence, and each unit ends with something the reader can do.

g.data-tip: The units are not three topics. They are the three things a position paper needs: an account of where the claim came from, an account of how the profession got its standing, and an account of what the evidence now supports. The course ends in a defended thesis rather than a survey.

Chapters 1 to 5. A weakly licensed medical marketplace, the adjustment of Harvey Lillard in Davenport in 1895 and the thin interested archive it descends from, the anatomical difficulty with the hearing claim, the rival lineages of Langworthy and Carver, and the straight and mixer schism.
g.text: back to its sources and say

g.data-tip: Chapters 6 to 10. Prosecutions endured as strategy, licensure creeping from Kansas in 1913 to Louisiana in 1974, the boycott built on a single ethical clause, Wilk v. AMA and the conspiracy it found, and the accreditation that gained federal recognition in the same year the containment campaign was dissolved.

Chapters 11 to 15. How differently the profession is regulated from one country to the next, technique systems and the reliability of the procedures that locate the lesion, the three unequal evidence bands, consent under contested risk, and the futures the profession has not chosen between.

g.data-hot: each unit assumes the one before
g.data-tip: The order is not decorative. The evidence chapters only land once you know how thin the founding archive is, and the modern ethics only land once you know that the famous legal victory was about conduct and expressly not about whether the treatment works.
g.text: each unit assumes the one before it
